subject: Post-demo: measurable TTFT targets and emit cadence for ShipFast pilot
snippet: TTFT targets: median <=120ms (p75), p95 <300ms; SSE chunk cadence every 150-250ms recommended; proposed pilot steps & measurement hooks.
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Park <daniel@shipfast.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 08 Jul 2026 15:12:00 -0400
Subject: Post-demo: measurable TTFT targets and emit cadence for ShipFast pilot

Hi Daniel — great demo today, thanks for the time. Quick written recap while items are fresh and to make the pilot asks explicit so your engineering team can review.

Context / goals
- Primary performance objective: reduce perceived latency in the fulfillment UI where users expect near-instant typing-style responses for quick lookups.
- Pilot throughput expectation: peak ~200 QPS, average 50 QPS; concurrency estimate ~40–60 connections during peak.

Proposed SLOs (suggested start point)
- Time-to-first-token (TTFT): median <= 120 ms; p75 <= 180 ms; p95 < 300 ms for 0–512 token prompts.
- End-to-end response for larger payloads (512–2k tokens): median <= 400 ms, p95 < 900 ms (we'll tune model selection).

Streaming / emit cadence notes
- Delivery: recommend SSE for your mobile/web clients (simpler reconnection semantics). WebSocket supported if you need long-lived multiplexing.
- Chunk cadence: suggest emitting small chunks every 150–250 ms for interactive UX; adjust after initial probe if you see jitter.

Operational asks for pilot
1) Provide a non-sensitive sample of representative prompt lengths and a synthetic traffic profile (CSV) so we can run an initial probe.
2) Confirm whether ShipFast prefers a single-region run (us-east) or multi-region from the start.
3) Assign an engineering point-of-contact for integration and a secondary contact for security/compliance docs.

Attachments: demo-recording.mp4 (short clip), SLO-table.csv (baseline targets + measurement plan).

Next steps
- If this sounds reasonable I'll set up a focused technical call with Karthik to walk the team through the probe plan and Redwood Console measurement hooks.
- Tentative timeline: probe next week, pilot (two-week run) the following week.

Thanks — Sergio
Sergio Alvarez
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
sergio@redwood.com

From: Daniel Park <daniel@shipfast.com>

Subject: Re: Post-demo: measurable TTFT targets and emit cadence for ShipFast pilot

Sergio — really helpful summary, thank you. A few clarifying questions from the engineering side: 

1) We operate with an EU storefront and a US storefront. Can the initial probe be single-region (us-east) with a straightforward plan to expand to eu-west within the pilot window? Or do you recommend testing both simultaneously?
2) For TTFT targets you listed, do those numbers assume a quantized 4-bit model or a float model? We have strict cost targets so if quantized variants materially change TTFT profiles we need to see that tradeoff.
3) Is SSE strictly preferred for reconnect logic? Our mobile SDKs have an established websocket layer — would switching to SSE be blocking for integration?
4) Pricing / credits for the pilot — any guidance so we can align procurement ahead of the pilot kickoff?

Attached: ShipFast-performance-priorities.pdf (internal prioritization doc).

I'm looping in our lead for the integration (on the eng@ address) who can pick a time for the deeper technical session.

— Daniel
Daniel Park
Head of Integrations, ShipFast
daniel@shipfast.com

From: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Park <daniel@shipfast.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 09 Jul 2026 08:17:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: measurable TTFT targets and emit cadence for ShipFast pilot

Daniel — quick technical reply to those questions so you have meat for your eng team: 

On regions
- Start single-region (us-east) for the first probe and pilot. We can template the same probe for eu-west within the second week — multi-region adds routing/fallback complexity but is straightforward.

On model variants and quantization
- The TTFT SLOs I suggested are for a production-optimized float16 variant on A100-class inference hardware. 4-bit quantized models generally reduce cost but may add 10–40 ms per TTFT depending on kernel choices and KV cache characteristics. We'll include quantization profiles in the pilot matrix.

On SSE vs WebSocket
- SSE is operationally simpler for short-lived request/response streaming (client reconnects are easier). WebSocket is fine if you need multiplexing across many streams per socket. Neither is blocking for integration — pick what matches your SDK surface, we can tune on our side.

Pilot measurement and tooling
- Proposed probe sequence (short):
  1) Synthetic baseline: replay representative prompts at low QPS to confirm kernel/sequence latency.
  2) Burst probe: ramp to peak QPS (200) to observe queuing and p95 behaviour.
  3) Realistic cadence run with client-side SSE chunks every 200ms to validate perceived UX and jitter.

- We'll expose per-request TTFT, per-route p50/p95, and chunk inter-arrival histograms in Redwood Console. We'll also provide a small instrumentation snippet (X-Request-ID propagation + timing hooks) for your side so traces line up.

Attachments and artifacts
- I'll drop a short pilot-plan.md into the Drive folder and link the HubSpot deal ID for reference.

Let us know an available 60-min slot for Friday (we have availability 11:00–15:00 ET) and we'll lock in the probe kickoff.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.com

Thanks Karthik / Sergio — this is great and addresses our concerns. Quick confirmations: 

- We approve starting single-region (us-east) for the initial probe with eu-west added in week two.
- We'll accept float16 baseline for the first run; include a side-by-side quantized run in the matrix so we can evaluate cost/latency tradeoffs.
- We'll use our existing WebSocket layer for now (not a blocker). We'll try SSE in the cadence run if you recommend it for the perceived UX.

Action items for both sides
- ShipFast: share representative prompts + traffic CSV by EOD Monday; procurement to review pilot pricing (I'll put Sergio in touch with our procurement lead).
- Redwood: drop pilot-plan.md and a short measurement runbook; share a preliminary cost ballpark for the two-week pilot.

We'll book your 60-min slot on Friday at 13:00 ET — Eng will join and we'll review the probe script.

Thanks — Daniel
